markets_note: Stocks were mixed in the latest snapshot: the S&P 500 fell 1.04 percent and the Nasdaq dropped 2.64 percent after a Thursday tech selloff, while the Dow rose 1.32 percent. The 10 year Treasury yield was 4.95 percent and the VIX was 19.25.

items.title: AM Best: Social Inflation Drives Surge in Commercial Auto Liability Claims
items.summary: AM Best reports that rising litigation costs, often called social inflation, keep pushing up commercial auto liability claims. Over 2014 to 2024, first year loss payments grew about 6.4 percent a year, compared with 2.8 percent for general inflation. Claims staying open longer adds exposure to jury awards, and the report says tort reform in Florida has helped bring average paid claim costs down.

items.title: Viewpoint: Generational Shifts, Delayed Projects Are Shaping Builder’s Risk
items.summary: An insurance executive's opinion piece says builder's risk insurance is being shaped by stalled projects, high loss ratios and a changing workforce. Tariffs and supply problems are delaying construction starts, and claims tend to show up many months after a policy begins. The writer also notes arson at developments is a major source of losses.

items.title: OSHA Proposes $648K in Fines for 6 Employers at New York Excavation Site
items.summary: The federal workplace safety agency has cited six New York and New Jersey employers for serious safety violations involving excavation hazards at a large mixed use construction site. The headline puts the proposed fines at $648,000 in total. Only the opening excerpt was available, so details are limited.

items.title: Procter & Gamble Q1 Earnings Call Highlights
items.summary: Procter and Gamble reported organic sales up 4 percent for its first fiscal quarter, led by volume growth, and kept its full year outlook. Core earnings per share were $2, up 1 percent, as higher commodity and freight costs cut into margins. Management warned those cost pressures are expected to build over the next several quarters.

items.title: International Business Machines (IBM) Just Gave Investors Something To Think About
items.summary: IBM reported third quarter revenue of $17.1 billion and adjusted earnings of $2.95 per share, both above Wall Street expectations. It kept its full year revenue growth outlook of 4 to 5 percent, raised its free cash flow outlook and held its quarterly dividend at $1.69. The article says the stock is up about 7.7 percent over the past week.

items.title: 'Big Short' Investor Michael Burry Bumps Up Substack Subscription Price, Flags 4 'Busted' Bear-Market Havens
items.summary: On Thursday, when tech stocks sold off, investor Michael Burry pointed to Adobe, Fiserv, Birkenstock and QXO as beaten down stocks that held up. Adobe rose 6.1 percent while the Nasdaq tracking fund fell 2.9 percent. He also raised his paid newsletter prices starting Nov. 1 and flagged a pending accounting proposal that could affect how Nvidia reports revenue.

items.title: An Elite Marathoner Blamed a Prescription for Her Positive Doping Test. The Problem? The ‘Doctor’ Who Wrote It Wasn’t a Doctor.
items.summary: Runner's World reports on elite marathoner Ruti Aga, who has stood on the podium at six World Marathon Majors and won the 2019 Tokyo Marathon. The headline says she blamed a prescription for a positive doping test, and that the person who wrote it was not a doctor. Only the opening excerpt was available.

items.summary: Belgian runners Merijn Geerts and Ivo Steyaert finished together to set a backyard ultra record for the third time, according to iRunFar. Only the opening excerpt was available, so details of the new mark are not included.
